PROPERTIES.player_hint_1_en: Only one square fits Cedric's clue ("He was in a corner of his area. He was beside the box and the crate."). So Cedric (C) must be at row 4, column 5. Cross out his row and column.
PROPERTIES.player_hint_2_en: Dora's clue ("She was beside a table in the Fish Market. She was in the Fish Market, but not beside the basket.") fits only one square. So Dora (D) must be at row 7, column 6. Cross out her row and column.
PROPERTIES.player_hint_3_en: Suppose Bert were at row 5, column 4: then Fiona would have nowhere left to go. So Bert can't be there. Bert can't be at row 6, column 2; row 6, column 3: in each case the general clue ("There was exactly one person in a rowboat.") could not be true. Using Albert's clue ("He was exactly one column west of Bert."), some squares are ruled out for Bert. So Bert (B) must be at row 5, column 2. Cross out his row and column.
PROPERTIES.player_hint_4_en: Suppose Fiona were at row 1, column 7: then Elsa would have nowhere left to go. So Fiona can't be there. Suppose Fiona were at row 3, column 7: then the general clue ("There was exactly one person in a rowboat.") could not be true. So Fiona can't be there. So Fiona (F) must be at row 6, column 3. Cross out her row and column.
PROPERTIES.player_hint_5_en: Elsa is now the only person who can still go in column 7. So Elsa (E) must be at row 1, column 7. Cross out her row and column.
PROPERTIES.player_hint_6_en: Using the general clue ("There was exactly one person in a rowboat."), some squares are ruled out for Valentine. So Valentine (the victim) must be at row 3, column 4. Cross out his row and column.
PROPERTIES.player_hint_7_en: With the rows and columns of everyone placed so far crossed out, only one square is left for Albert that fits his clue ("He was exactly one column west of Bert."). So Albert (A) must be at row 2, column 1. Cross out his row and column. Cedric is the only person in the Shipyard with Valentine, so Cedric is the murderer!
